slides.heading: Flatten Binary Tree
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Flatten Binary Tree, a very hard binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Rewire the tree in place into a doubly linked list in in-order order (left = prev, right = next); return the leftmost node.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Rewire the tree in place into a doubly linked list in in-order order (left equals prev, right equals next); return the leftmost node.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: In-order linking: each subtree returns its leftmost and rightmost nodes so neighbours can be connected.
slides.narration: In-order linking: each subtree returns its leftmost and rightmost nodes so neighbours can be connected.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: In-order into an array, then relink → O(n) space
slides.narration: Collecting nodes in order and relinking uses linear space. Returning both ends of each flattened subtree lets us link in place with only the recursion stack.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Link left's rightmost to the node
3. Link the node to right's leftmost
slides.narration: Step by step. First, flatten left and right recursively. Second, link left's rightmost to the node. Third, link the node to right's leftmost. Fourth, return the outer ends.

slides.caption: Recursively return both ends
slides.narration: Each call returns the leftmost and rightmost of its flattened subtree, so the parent can link its left list's tail and right list's head to itself.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Result: 4 ⇄ 2 ⇄ 5 ⇄ 1 ⇄ 6 ⇄ 3
slides.narration: The result is four, two, five, one, six, three, linked both ways.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Flatten recurses left, links its rightmost to the node, recurses right, links its leftmost to the node, and returns the outer ends.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Return the leftmost as the new head
slides.narration: Return the leftmost node as the head.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: In-order linking: each subtree returns its leftmost and rightmost nodes so neighbours can be connected.
slides.narration: To recap Flatten Binary Tree: In-order linking: each subtree returns its leftmost and rightmost nodes so neighbours can be connected. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
